# 1 Maccabees Chapter 13 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_013_page_001.jpg

---

**1** When Simon heard that Trypho had assembled a large army to come into the land of Judea and destroy it,

**2** and saw that the people were trembling with fear, he went up to Jerusalem and gathered the people together.

**3** He encouraged them and spoke to them: "You know all that my brothers and I and my father's house have done for the sake of the laws and the sanctuary — all the wars we have fought and all the hardships we have endured.

**4** For this cause all my brothers have died for Israel's sake, and I alone am left.

**5** Far be it from me to spare my own life in any time of tribulation, for I am no better than my brothers.

**6** Rather I will avenge my nation and the sanctuary and your wives and children, for all the nations have gathered to destroy us out of pure hatred."

**7** The spirit of the people revived as they heard these words.

**8** They answered in a great voice: "You are our leader in place of Judas and Jonathan your brothers.

**9** Fight our battles! Whatever you command us, we will do."

**10** He mustered all the fighting men and hastened to complete the walls of Jerusalem and to fortify it all around.

**11** He sent Jonathan son of Absalom with a considerable force to Joppa; Jonathan expelled the inhabitants and stayed there.

**12** When Trypho moved to invade the land with a large army and encamped at Adora, Simon kept pace with him, moving wherever he went.

**13** And Trypho encamped against Baskama.

**14** Seeing that Simon had come to Jonathan's place, Trypho sent word to Simon:

**15** "Your brother Jonathan is held by us because of the hundred talents of silver he owed the royal treasury on account of the offices he held, and because of two sons whom he left with us as hostages.

**16** Send us one hundred talents of silver and his two sons, and we will release him; otherwise we will not release him."

**17** Simon knew that this was being said to him in deceit, yet he ordered the silver and the boys to be sent lest he provoke great hostility among the people,

**18** who might say: "It was because he would not send the money and the boys that Jonathan died."

**19** He sent the boys and the hundred talents — and Trypho kept his word no further and did not release Jonathan.

**20** After that, Trypho moved to invade and ravage the country, taking the road by way of Adora; and Simon and his army shadowed him at every turn.

**21** Meanwhile the men in the citadel sent word to Trypho, urging him to come to them by way of the wilderness and to send them provisions.

**22** Trypho prepared all his cavalry to march, but that night an exceptionally heavy snowfall came, and he was unable to advance because of the snow; he therefore withdrew and went into Gilead.

**23** When he came near Baskama, he killed Jonathan, who was buried there.

**24** Then Trypho turned back and returned to his own land.

**25** Simon sent and recovered the bones of Jonathan his brother and buried him at Modein, the city of his ancestors.

**26** All Israel mourned him with great lamentation for many days.

**27** Simon built a monument over the tomb of his father and his brothers, making it high enough to be seen; it was faced with polished stone on the front and back.

**28** He erected seven pyramids facing one another, for his father, his mother, and his four brothers.

**29** For the pyramids he fashioned great columns, and on the columns he placed suits of armor as an everlasting memorial; beside the armor he carved ships, so that they could be seen by all who sail the sea.

**30** This is the tomb he made at Modein, and it stands to this day.

**31** Trypho dealt treacherously with the young King Antiochus and murdered him,

**32** and became king in his place, put on the crown of Asia, and brought great calamity on the land.

**33** Simon rebuilt the strongholds of Judea, surrounding them with high towers and great walls, with gates and bars, and stored provisions in the strongholds.

**34** Simon also chose envoys and sent them to King Demetrius requesting him to grant the country relief from taxation, because all that Trypho was doing was plundering it.

**35** King Demetrius sent him this reply:

**36** "King Demetrius to Simon the high priest and Friend of Kings, and to the elders and to the Jewish nation, greetings.

**37** The golden crown and the palm branch that you sent, we have received; and we are prepared to conclude a full peace with you and to write to the royal officials to grant you relief.

**38** Whatever we have already confirmed to you, remains confirmed; and the strongholds that you have built shall be yours.

**39** We pardon all the offenses and faults committed up to this day, and remit the crown tax that you owe; and whatever other levy was formerly collected in Jerusalem shall be collected no more.

**40** Any of you who are qualified for enrolment in our service, let them be enrolled; and let there be peace between us."

**41** In the one hundred and seventieth year the yoke of the Gentiles was lifted from Israel,

**42** and the people began to write in their documents and contracts: "In the first year of Simon, the great high priest, commander, and leader of the Jews."

**43** In those days he encamped against Gazara and surrounded it with his troops; he constructed a siege engine, brought it up against the city, breached a tower, and captured it.

**44** The men in the engine leaped down into the city, and a great tumult broke out.

**45** The men of the city went up on the walls — women and children with them — tore their clothes and cried out in a great voice, pleading with Simon to give them his right hand of peace;

**46** and they said: "Do not treat us according to our wickedness, but according to your mercy."

**47** Simon relented and stopped fighting against them. He expelled them from the city and purified the houses in which the idols had been set up; then he entered the city with songs of praise and blessing.

**48** He removed all defilement from it and settled in it men who observed the law; he strengthened it and made it his own residence.

**49** Those in the Jerusalem citadel were kept from going out to the countryside, and from buying and selling; they were in severe want, and many of them died of hunger.

**50** They cried out to Simon to accept their surrender, and he gave them his right hand. He expelled them from the citadel and cleansed it from its pollutions.

**51** On the twenty-third day of the second month, in the one hundred and seventy-first year, he entered the citadel with praise and waving of palm branches, with harps and cymbals and lutes, with hymns and songs, because a great enemy had been trampled down out of Israel.

**52** He ordained that this day should be observed every year with joy and gladness. And he strengthened the temple mount which stood beside the citadel, and he and his companions lived there.

**53** Simon saw that his son John was now grown to manhood, and he appointed him commander of all the forces; and John lived at Gazara.
